rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، عكرمة، قتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Ikrima, and Qatada classify the seven-verse sura as Meccan.
rows.anchor: قيل: مكية، عن ابن عباس، والحسن، وعكرمة، وقتادة

rows.speaker: الضحاك، الواقدي
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Waqidi classify the sura as Medinan.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مدنية، عن الضحاك، والواقدي

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says it is Meccan through the mention of the needy, with the remainder Medinan.
rows.anchor: مكية إلى قوله: (المسكين) وباقي السورة مدنية، عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report transmitted from Ubayy says reciting this sura brings God's forgiveness for one who pays zakat; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي، عن النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (أرأيت) غفر الله له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting favors to Quraysh, the sura marvels at their conduct despite Meccan security and provision, then their denial of the Prophet and his prophethood.
rows.anchor: افتتح هذه السورة تعجبا من حالهم مع عظم النعم عليهم بمكة من الأمن والرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading yaduʿ has a doubled ʿayn and means to push away forcefully.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: (يدع) بضم الدال وتشديد العين من الدع، وهو الدفع

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
rows.claim: Abu Raja reads yaduʿ with an open dal and light ʿayn, meaning to leave or abandon, from wadaʿa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء العطاردي: يدع بفتح الدال، وتخفيف العين أي: يترك، من قولهم: ودعته أي: تركته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that Arabic lacks this verb's past tense and verbal noun is false; the Prophet's wording uses wadaʿ as a noun for leaving Friday prayer.
rows.anchor: فقد ورد في الحديث: لينتهين الناس عن ودعهم الجمعات أو ليختمن على قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's waddaʿahu means that he left his beloved, further attesting the verb.
rows.anchor: غاله في الحب حتى ودعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-din can mean recompense, reckoning, the professed way, obedience, or custom; its root sense is recompense.
rows.anchor: الدين: الجزاء، والدين: الحساب، والدين: ما يدان به، والدين: الطاعة، والدين: العادة، وأصل الباب: الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-daʿ means forceful pushing; related uses evoke shaking a measure to fill it, urging an unsteady person, or driving goats.
rows.anchor: الدع: الدفع بشدة، دععته دعا، ودعه يدعه دعا: إذا دفعته دفعا شديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root also appears in moving a measure so it fills, telling someone who stumbles daʿ daʿ, and as a goatherd's urging sound.
rows.anchor: الدعدعة: تحريكك المكيال ليستوعب الشيء، كأنه يدفعه

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil distinguishes urging in travel or driving from exhortation: ḥath applies to movement and other matters, while ḥaḍḍ is not used for travel or driving.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل: الفرق بين الحث والحض أن الحث يكون في السير والسوق وكل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After swearing by specified nights, God swears by night generally as it passes, as in two other night oaths.
rows.anchor: وبعد ما أقسم بالليالي المخصوصة أقسم بالليل على العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form al-watr with fatḥa on waw is a dialect variant; al-tirah is only pronounced with kasra.
rows.anchor: بفتح الواو ،   وهما لغتان كالحبر والحبر في العدد

rows.speaker: يونس عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: Yunus reports from Abu Amr a reading of al-watr with waw fatḥa and tāʾ kasra.
rows.anchor: بفتح الواو وكسر التاء : رواها يونس عن أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading joins al-fajr with al-watr.
rows.anchor: قرىء «والفجر » والوتر ،   ويسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwin on yasri substitutes for the extended alif of poetic-style vowel lengthening.
rows.anchor: ويسر : بالتنوين ،   وهو التنوين الذي يقع بدلاً من حرف الإطلاق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the ten nights in a genitive construction, meaning nights of ten days.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : وليال عشر ،   بالإضافة يريد : وليال أيام عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ in yasri drops in connected speech because the kasra suffices, and at pause both the yāʾ and kasra drop.
rows.anchor: وياء { يَسْرِ } تحذف في الدرج ،   اكتفاء عنها بالكسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation supplies a preposition: the night travels within it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : معنى «يسري » يسري فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath concerns the previously sworn objects; the question asks whether a rational person should regard them as worthy of exaltation by oath.
rows.anchor: أي فيما أقسمت به من هذه الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the question asks whether this is a great oath suitable to confirm the matter being sworn to.
rows.anchor: هل هو قسم عظيم يؤكد بمثله المقسم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥijr means intellect because it restrains a person from heedless conduct, like ʿaql and nuhyah; ḥaṣāh derives from counting and control.
rows.anchor: لأنه يحجر عن التهافت فيما لا ينبغي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says a person of ḥijr is one who masters and disciplines himself.
rows.anchor: إذا كان قاهراً لنفسه ضابطاً لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted oath answer is that God will punish them, as the later threat of a scourge of punishment indicates.
rows.anchor: يدل عليه قوله : { أَلَمْ تَرَ }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing Hell is comparable to the verse saying that Hell is exposed.
rows.anchor: كقوله : { وَبُرّزَتِ الجحيم }

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says this verse changed the Prophet's face; when Ali asked how Hell would be brought, the Prophet said 70,000 angels would lead it on 70,000 reins, and it could break loose and burn the assembly; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: يجيء بها سبعون ألف ملك يقودونها بسبعين ألف زمام ،   فتشرد شردة لو تركت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human remembers what he neglected, or takes warning from it.
rows.anchor: أي : يتذكر ما فرط فيه ،   أو يتعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means that remembrance will not benefit him; an omitted genitive must be supplied, or the paired clauses would conflict.
rows.anchor: ومن أين له منفعة الذكرى ؟ لا بد من تقدير حذف المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For my life may mean the afterlife, or the time of my worldly life, as in dating an event to nights of Rajab; the latter is clearer.
rows.anchor: وهي حياة الآخرة ،   أو وقت حياتي في الدنيا ،   كقولك : جئته لعشر ليال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The regret proves people had choice through their intentions and wills and were not prevented from obedience or compelled to sin, as some heretical schools claim.
rows.anchor: وهذا أبين دليل على أن الاختيار كان في أيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabad originally describes a painful, swollen liver, then broadened to every hardship and exertion; mukābadah derives from it.
rows.anchor: والكبد : أصله من قولك : كبد الرجل كبداً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb kabata, meaning to destroy, likewise originates in striking someone's liver.
rows.anchor: كما قيل : كبته بمعى أهلكه . وأصله : كبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf cites Labid's word kabad to mean the severity of the affair and the difficulty of its crisis.
rows.anchor: قُمْنَا وَقَامَ الْخُصُومُ فِي كَبَدِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Freeing a neck means releasing it from slavery or another restraint.
rows.anchor: تخليصها من رق أو غيره

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet distinguishes emancipating someone outright from helping free them from retaliation or debt; this was his answer to a man's question about entering Paradise.
rows.anchor: أن تعين في تخليصها . من قود أو غرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emancipation and charity are among the most excellent deeds.
rows.anchor: والعتق والصدقة : من أفاضل الأعمال

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa holds emancipation more virtuous than charity.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه : أن العتق أفضل من الصدقة

rows.speaker: صاحبا أبي حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa's two companions hold charity more virtuous than emancipation.
rows.anchor: وعند صاحبيه : الصدقة أفضل والآية أدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's ordering, naming emancipation before feeding, better supports Abu Hanifa's ranking.
rows.anchor: والآية أدل على قول أبي حنيفة لتقديم العتق الصدقة

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says freeing a slave is better than giving surplus money to a relative, citing the Prophet's promise that God frees a limb from Fire for every limb released.
rows.anchor: أو يعتق رقبة ؟ قال : الرقبة أفضل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says whoever frees a slave, God frees one of his limbs from the Fire for each limb of the slave.
rows.anchor: من فك رقبة فك الله بكل عضو منها عضواً منه من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading treats 'freeing a neck or feeding' as a nominal explanation: it is emancipation or feeding.
rows.anchor: على : هي فك رقبة ،   أو إطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading uses the verb 'feed' as an alternative to 'free a neck,' parsing it as a substitute for 'climb the steep path.'
rows.anchor: أو أطعم ،   على الإبدال من اقتحم العقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masghabah derives from hunger, maqrabah from kinship, and matrabah from poverty and being stuck to the earth; atraba means becoming rich, like athra.
rows.anchor: مفعلات من سغب : إذا جاع . وقرب في النسب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet explains a person of matrabah as someone whose home is a rubbish dump.
rows.anchor: في قوله : { ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ } الذي مأواه المزابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing a day as possessing hunger follows the grammatical pattern of saying that someone is 'possessed of toil.'
rows.anchor: ووصف اليوم بذي مسغبة نحو ما

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads the phrase with accusative dhā masghabah, governed by feeding, meaning food on a hunger-stricken day.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : «ذا مسغبة » نصبه بإطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon follows the sun by rising as it sets and taking its light, during the first half of the month.
rows.anchor: طالعاً عند غروبها آخذاً من نورها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, when the moon becomes full it follows the sun in brightness and light.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إذا استدار فتلاها في الضياء والنور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day reveals the sun as it expands, when the sun becomes fully visible.
rows.anchor: عند انتفاخ النهار وانبساطه ،   لأن الشمس تنجلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to darkness, the world, or the earth, although earth was not previously mentioned; ordinary speech similarly omits understood referents such as morning or sky.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الضمير للظلمة ،   أو للدنيا ،   أو للأرض ،   وإن لم يجر لها ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night covers its referent until it disappears and the horizons grow dark.
rows.anchor: إذا يغشاها ،   فتغيب وتظلم الآفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative of idhā is difficult: coordination seems to govern both accusative and genitive, while treating each wāw as oath conflicts with al-Khalil and Sibawayh's aversion.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت : الأمر في نصب «إذا » معضل : لأنك لا تخلو إما أن تجعل الواوات عاطفة فتنصب بها وتجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath wāw suppresses the verb and itself stands in its place, unlike bāʾ, which replaces both verb and preposition; coordinated wāws can therefore govern both cases, as in a verb's coordination.
rows.anchor: أن واو القسم مطرح معها إبراز الفعل إطراحاً كلياً ، فكان لها شأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day becomes manifest when night darkness vanishes.
rows.anchor: تجلى } ظهر بزوال ظلمة الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, daylight becomes clear and uncovered as the sun rises.
rows.anchor: أو تبين وتكشف بطلوع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shattā is the plural of shatīt: people's pursuits are diverse, as the following verses explain.
rows.anchor: جمع شتيت ،   أي : إن مساعيكم أشتات مختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving means paying one's financial obligations, and fearing God means refraining from disobedience.
rows.anchor: يعني حقوق ماله { واتقى } الله فلم يعصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥusnā may mean the good quality of faith, the good religion of Islam, or the good reward of Paradise.
rows.anchor: بالخصلة الحسنى : وهي الإيمان . أو بالملة الحسنى : وهي ملة الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusirr means to prepare someone, by analogy with making a horse ready for riding by saddling and bridling it.
rows.anchor: فسنهيؤه لها من يسر الفرس للركوب إذا أسرجها وألجمها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says each person is facilitated toward what he was created for.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : « كل ميسر لما خلق له »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will gently guide and enable the person until obedience becomes easiest, as when God opens someone's heart to Islam.
rows.anchor: والمعنى فسنلطف به ونوفقه حتى تكون الطاعة أيسر الأمور عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura is Meccan and contains eleven verses.
rows.anchor: مكية وآياتها إحدى عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḍuḥā is the forenoon, from the start of day until the sun rises high and spreads its rays.
rows.anchor: وهو صدر النهار حتى ترتفع الشمس وتلقي شعاعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view singles out forenoon because Moses spoke and the magicians prostrated then, supported by the call to gather people at forenoon.
rows.anchor: الساعة التي كلم فيها موسى عليه السلام ،   وألقي فيها السحرة سجداً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes al-ḍuḥā to mean daytime, as in the verse contrasting punishment by forenoon with punishment by night.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أريد بالضحى : النهار ،   بيانه قوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sajā describes darkness as settled and still.
rows.anchor: سجى } سكون وركد ظلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A calm night may be called sājin; the root also describes settled sea waves and a steady, languid eye.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ليلة ساجية ساكنة الريح . وقيل معناه : سكن الناس والأصوات فيه . وسجا البحر : سكنت أمواجه . وطرف ساج : ساكن فاتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that people and sounds become quiet during the night.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه : سكن الناس والأصوات فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause answers the oath and means God has not abandoned the Prophet like someone who takes leave.
rows.anchor: جواب القسم . ومعناه : ما قطعك قطع المودع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lighter reading of waddaʿaka means simply that God did not leave the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالتخفيف ،   يعني : ما تركك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem's verb waddaʿnā means 'we left,' evidence for the usage of wadaʿ.
rows.anchor: وَثَمَّ وَدَّعْنَا آلَ عَمْرٍو وَعَامِرٍ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawdiʿ intensifies leaving: a person who bids farewell while departing has emphatically left you.
rows.anchor: مبالغة في الودع ؛ لأنّ من ودّعك مفارقاً فقد بالغ في تركك

rows.speaker: المشركون
rows.claim: When revelation was delayed for days, the polytheists said Muhammad's Lord had abandoned and hated him.
rows.anchor: فقال المشركون : إنّ محمداً ودّعه ربه وقلاه

rows.speaker: أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب
rows.claim: Another occasion report says Umm Jamil told Muhammad that his devil had left him, after which the sura was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنّ أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب قالت له : يا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun is omitted after qalā, as in al-dhākirāt and the shortened sequence 'sheltered, guided, enriched,' because the omitted object is obvious.
rows.anchor: في قوله : { والذاكرين الله كثيراً والذاكرات }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'With' presents relief as accompanying hardship by drawing near the ease God will bring soon, consoling people and strengthening their hearts.
rows.anchor: بزمان قريب ،   فقرّب اليسر المترقب حتى جعله كالمقارن للعسر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud say hardship cannot overcome two eases; the statement is also reported as a prophetic saying.
rows.anchor: قول ابن عباس وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهما : لن يغلب عسر يسرين

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet once came out laughing and declared that hardship would not overcome two eases; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: ذات يوم وهو يضحك ويقول : « لن يغلب عسر يسرين »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saying follows the apparent wording and strong hope, taking God's promise in its fullest and most generous sense.
rows.anchor: على الظاهر ،   وبناء على قوّة الرجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated sentence may simply reinforce the first promise in people's hearts, like repeating the warning 'woe that day to the deniers.'
rows.anchor: لتقرير معناها في النفوس وتمكينها في القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the first sentence promises ease after their known hardship and the second gives a fresh promise of further ease, yielding two eases.
rows.anchor: والثانية عدة مستأنفة بأن العسر متبوع بيسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite singular hardship is one hardship whether it refers to their known affliction or to hardship as a familiar kind.
rows.anchor: وهو العسر الذي كانوا فيه ،   فهو هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two eases may be victories during the Prophet's lifetime and the caliphs' eras, or ease in this world and the next, like the two good outcomes in another verse.
rows.anchor: ما تيسر لهم في أيام الخلفاء ،   وأن يراد يسر الدنيا ويسر الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite yusran conveys magnification: the promised ease is immense and extraordinary.
rows.anchor: إن مع العسر يسراً عظيماً وأيّ يسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masud's codex has the ease clause only once.
rows.anchor: وهو في مصحف ابن مسعود مرة واحدة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that if hardship were in a lizard's hole, ease would seek it out, and hardship would not overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: لو كان العسر في جحر لطلبه اليسر حتى يدخل عليه ،   إنه لن يغلب عسر يسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's two eases can be understood as the magnified ease in the verse applied to both abodes, making two in reality despite Ibn Masud's single written occurrence.
rows.anchor: فتأوله بيسر الدارين ،   وذلك يسران في الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is created with the best balanced form, shape, and arrangement of limbs.
rows.anchor: في أحسن تعديل لشكله وصورته وتسوية لأعضائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because people failed to thank God for their excellent creation, they may be returned lower than the lowest in form, as ugly and misshapen people of Hell, or to the lowest ranks of Hell.
rows.anchor: حين لم يشكر نعمة تلك الخلقة الحسنة القويمة السوية : أن رددناه أسفل من سفل خلقاً وتركيباً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God returns people below their former beauty through old age: bent backs, white hair, wrinkled skin, weakened senses and strength, slow gait, faint voice, and senility.
rows.anchor: فقوس ظهره بعد اعتداله ،   وابيض شعره بعد سواده ،   وتشنن جلده

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abd Allah reads the phrase as 'the lowest of the low.'
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله : «أسفل السافلين »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception connects grammatically under the first interpretation of the preceding verse, but is disconnected under the second.
rows.anchor: هو على الأول متصل ظاهر الاتصال ،   وعلى الثاني : منقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous elderly people receive unending reward for obedience, patience through God's trial of aging, and worship despite weakened ability to rise.
rows.anchor: ولكن الذين كانوا صالحين من الهرمى فلهم ثواب دائم غير منقطع على طاعتهم وصبرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The horses strike stones with their hooves and kindle sparks, called the fire of al-ḥabāḥib.
rows.anchor: توري نار الحباحب ،   وهي ما ينقدح من حوافرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadḥ means striking, while īrāʾ means producing fire; one may strike and kindle or strike without a spark.
rows.anchor: والقدح : الصك . والإيراء : إخراج النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative qadḥan is governed by the same element that governs ḍabḥan in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: وانتصب قدحاً بما انتصب به ضبحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raiders attack the enemy at dawn.
rows.anchor: تغير على العدوّ { صُبْحاً } في وقت الصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At that time the horses stir up dust.
rows.anchor: نقعاً ( 4 ) } فهيجن بذلك الوقت غباراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasatna bihi may mean they reached the enemy's midst at that time or by means of the dust, or that they were enveloped in it.
rows.anchor: فوسطن به } بذلك الوقت ،   أو بالنقع ،   أي : وسطن النقع الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawāzīn may be the plural of 'weighed thing,' meaning deeds of weight and worth before God, or a plural of 'scale.'
rows.anchor: جمع موزون ،   وهو العمل الذي له وزن وخطر عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavy scales mean that the good deeds outweigh the bad.
rows.anchor: وثقلها : رجحانها . ومنه حديث أبي بكر

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: In advice to Umar, Abu Bakr says truth-followers gain heavy scales and falsehood-followers light ones, as each scale appropriately holds only good deeds or only sins.
rows.anchor: في وصيته له : «وإنما ثقلت موازين من ثقلت موازينهم يوم القيامة باتباعهم الحق

none: The segment contains only the verse text.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says people visited graves while boasting, pointing out whose grave was whose.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانوا يزورون المقابر فيقولون : هذا قبر فلان وهذا قبر فلان عند تفاخرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their rivalry distracted them with something useless in this life and the next, away from the more important work of religion.
rows.anchor: وهو مما لا يعينكم ولا يجدي عليكم في دنياكم وآخرتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, pursuit and rivalry over wealth and children consume life until death and burial, diverting people from preparing for the next life; visiting graves is a metaphor for death.
rows.anchor: أو أراد ألهاكم التكاثر بالأموال والأولاد إلى أن متم وقبرتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first cited poem uses visiting the grave as the endpoint of a year, supporting the metaphor of death.
rows.anchor: لَنْ يُخْلِصَ الْعَامَ خَلِيلٌ عِشْراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second poetic line about Abu Malik visiting graves likewise illustrates grave-visiting as death.
rows.anchor: زَارَ الْقُبُورَ أَبُو مَالِكٍ *** فَأَصْبَحَ أَلأمَّ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the opening with an interrogative hamza, whose question serves to assert the rebuke.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس : «أألهاكم » ؟ على الاستفهام الذي معناه التقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān refers to humanity as a class.
rows.anchor: والإنسان : للجنس . والخسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khusr means loss, just as kufr can mean kufrān.
rows.anchor: والخسر : الخسران ،   كما قيل : الكفر في الكفران
